Hi Laura — thanks for the report and for attaching the .eml+screenshot. Sorry for the trouble. A few quick clarifying questions and steps while we triage: 

1) Can you paste the full invite URL (the long ariba.redwood link) — sometimes corporate proxy/IDP rewrites subdomains or strips relayState values.
2) If possible, try the link in an Incognito window (no extensions) and also from a different network (personal hotspot) — that'll help rule out a corporate proxy.
3) Do you have an internal SSO admin who can check Okta logs for a failed assertion around the time you clicked the link? The failure mode you described matches an assertion-mismatch where relayState was truncated and the IDP returns a 403.

Workaround (quick): If you can share the full invite URL I can generate a one-time accept link (tenant-claim fallback) that bypasses the usual relayState. That will let Borealis finish vendor setup while we dig into why the IDP is rewriting the redirect.

Ben — I’m copying you and Monica. Can you review the attached .eml and screenshot and look for any redirect headers or extra query params in the invite token that might be hitting corporate IDP guards? If we confirm relayState loss we should add a compact-claim fallback for Ariba invites for orgs that front with restrictive Okta proxy rules.

Laura — once you reply with the URL I’ll issue the one-time accept link. If you prefer, I can also schedule a 20 minute screen-share with your IT team to pull Okta debug logs.

Best,
David Kim

https://ariba.redwoodinference.com/invite/accept?token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6Ij...&relayState=https%3A%2F%2Fokta.borealis.com%2Fapp%2Fsomething%3Fstate%3Dxyz%26return_to%3Dhttps%253A%252F%252Fariba.redwoodinference.com%252Fcallback

We tried incognito and personal hotspot — still 403. Our Okta admin pulled logs and sees an inbound redirect with a missing relayState parameter (looks truncated after URL-encoding). I attached a short network trace (redirect-trace.txt) — you can see the relayState value gets split by a proxy rewrite rule at our edge.

Workaround success: David generated a one-time accept link and I used it to finish the onboarding steps — vendor profile now shows active. However, we'd like a durable fix so future invites don't require one-off links.

Request: Can Redwood add a compact-claim accept mode for Ariba invites (shorter token + server-side association) or a retry that reconstructs relayState if the IDP returns a partial assertion? Ben/Monica — happy to jump on a call to review logs.
